jsonld.name: Proper Café Fry-Up
jsonld.description: The working café's version — the plate that has to be on the pass ninety seconds after it's ordered, cooked on a griddle that has been seasoned since Margaret Thatcher, and served with the particular crisp-edged, well-basted character that only repetition produces. This recipe reverse-engineers the caff's system for the home kitchen: a flat griddle or heavy pan run at two temperatures, a strict component order, beans from a pan not a microwave, and the small professional habits — back bacon pressed flat, sausages with one prick, eggs basted, fried bread from the bacon's fat — that make the difference. The café fry-up differs from the full English master in one key respect: speed. Where the full English's architecture optimises for quality with time to spare, the café method optimises for the plate landing hot in minutes — hotter pan, faster sequence, everything landing inside 25 minutes with the tea still steeping.

skeleton:
Proper Café Fry-Up

British · Medium · Serves 2

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The working café's version — the plate that has to be on the pass ninety seconds after it's ordered, cooked on a griddle that has been seasoned since Margaret Thatcher, and served with the particular crisp-edged, well-basted character that only repetition produces. This recipe reverse-engineers the caff's system for the home kitchen: a flat griddle or heavy pan run at two temperatures, a strict component order, beans from a pan not a microwave, and the small professional habits — back bacon pressed flat, sausages with one prick, eggs basted, fried bread from the bacon's fat — that make the difference. The café fry-up differs from the full English master in one key respect: speed. Where the full English's architecture optimises for quality with time to spare, the café method optimises for the plate landing hot in minutes — hotter pan, faster sequence, everything landing inside 25 minutes with the tea still steeping.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The works, café portions

  • the caff's default, pressed flat

Fat and seasoning

  • the bottles, to serve
- **The two-temperature doctrine:** the caff griddle runs a hot half and a cooler half. At home, this means one pan started hot (sausages, fried bread) and dropped to medium (bacon, eggs), with a small pan for the beans alongside. Heat control is the caff cook's entire craft. - **Everything out of the fridge 20 minutes ahead** — cold sausage on a hot griddle seizes and cooks unevenly; the caff's ingredients sit at room temperature by necessity and law. - **Warm plates in a 110 °C oven.** The café plate lands hot because the plate itself is hot — a cold plate loses five degrees of crisp in ten seconds. Two plates, lowest shelf, from the start. - The beans go in a small pan with the milk or butter — never the microwave's rubbery edge — and simmer while everything else cooks.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • Sausages: all-four-sides brown, once-pricked, clear juices.
  • Bacon: pressed flat at contact; glassy amber fat, uncurled.
  • Fried bread: taken early enough to stay bread, not crouton.
  • Eggs: basted, lace-edged, running yolks; plate assembled hot with zones respected.

Proper Café Fry-Up

Prep: 10 minutes · Cook: 25 minutes · Total: 35 minutes · Serves 2

Ingredients

The works, café portions

  • 4 pork sausages (320 g), pricked once each
  • 4 rashers (200 g) unsmoked back bacon — the caff's default, pressed flat
  • 4 thick slices (200 g) black pudding
  • 4 large eggs (220 g)
  • 2 slices (100 g) thick white bread, for fried bread
  • 200 g baked beans (half a tin)
  • 1 large tomato (150 g), halved, or 100 g tinned plum tomato, drained (the winter caff option)
  • 100 g button mushrooms, whole if small

Fat and seasoning

  • 15 ml / 14 g neutral oil, to start
  • 15 g butter
  • 3 g fine sea salt
  • 1 g white pepper (the café's quiet signature)
  • 15 ml milk or 10 g butter, for the beans
  • Brown breakfast sauce and tomato ketchup sachets' honest superiors — the bottles, to serve
  • Strong builder's tea, to drink

Instructions

  1. **Sausages hot, 8–10 minutes.** Film the pan with the oil over medium-high heat and lay in the sausages. Cook 8–10 minutes, turning every 2–3 minutes to brown all four sides, dropping the heat to medium after the first turn. Checkpoint — deeply browned on every face, skins taut (one pin-prick vent), juices running clear at a nick. The pan holds its first slick of rendered fat — the fry's first currency.
  2. **Fried bread — the fat's first dividend, 3 minutes.** Lay the bread straight into the pan's fat, pressing it flat with the spatula so it drinks evenly. Fry 90 seconds a side until deep gold and crisp-edged, then lift to the warm plate. Checkpoint — the bread is evenly golden, crisp at the surface but still faintly yielding within — fried bread, not a crouton. Any fat left in the pan stays; the bacon needs it next.
  3. **Bacon flat, 5 minutes.** Lay the bacon rashers in the hot fat and immediately press them flat with the spatula for 10 seconds — the caff's trick against curling. Cook 2–3 minutes until the underside renders glassy-gold, flip, and cook 2 minutes more. Add the black pudding slices and mushrooms to the pan's free space for the last 4 minutes, turning the pudding once and the mushrooms as they brown. Checkpoint — the bacon is flat, its fat glassy and amber, the eye just-set and juicy; the black pudding is dark-crusted both faces, holding firm; the mushrooms have browned and glossed in the accumulated fat. The tomato halves go cut-face down for the final 2 minutes, just to blister and heat.
  4. **Eggs basted, 2–3 minutes — the fry's finale.** Clear the pan's centre (cooked items rest at the edges or join the warm plates), add the butter to the fat, and crack in the eggs when it foams. Cook 90 seconds, tilting the pan and spooning the hot fat over the whites repeatedly, until the whites set with lace edges and the yolks stay liquid. Checkpoint — whites fully set — top and bottom — with golden frilled edges, yolks domed and running. Basted eggs are the café egg: no flipped yolk-cracking risk, no lid-sogginess, one pan's worth of fat doing all of it.
  5. **The plate — assembly in the caff's order.** Beans first, poured to one side of each hot plate (their sauce must not meet the egg). Then, clockwise from twelve: egg, bacon crossed, sausages, black pudding, mushrooms, tomato, and the fried bread propped at the edge. White pepper over the eggs — the café's quiet signature — and the sauce bottles on the table. Checkpoint — the plate at arm's length reads as *a proper fry-up* — full, browned, separated zones, yolk intact; and every component is still at eating temperature because the plates were hot and the sequence was fast.

Finish & Plate

The full works with builder's tea — strong, milky, the mug refilled before asked. Brown sauce for the bacon and fried bread, ketchup for the sausage, and the fork worked from the egg outward, each component dipped or dragged through its proper sauce. This is the plate eaten standing at the counter or sitting at the window, in under ten minutes, entirely without regret.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Bacon curled and ridgedNo press at contactThe 10-second flat press, immediately
Fried bread greasy and heavyPan's fat too deep or bread left too long90 seconds a side; pour off excess fat first
Sausages burst and greyPricked repeatedly or heat spikedOne prick, medium after the first turn
Everything tepid by platingCold plates, slow sequencePlates in the oven from minute one; the fry's pace is part of the recipe
Beans developed a skin or rubbery edgeMicrowavedSmall pan, splash of milk, gentle simmer, stir once

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **The caff doesn't do make-ahead, and neither does this plate** — it is a 35-minute, eat-immediately dish by design. Components keep 3 days refrigerated if leftovers insist on existing; the eggs never do. - **Variation — the "number 4" plate:** any café's menu is this master with components subtracted — two eggs, bacon, sausage, beans, fried bread is the most-ordered plate in Britain. The sequencing holds for any subset. - **Variation — the large plate ("the works plus"):** add a slice of fried bread and a second egg; the pan's sequence stretches by 3 minutes at the egg stage only. - **The griddle upgrade:** a cast-iron double-burner griddle run hot at one end and cooler at the other is the honest home replica of the caff's two-temperature system, and turns this recipe from skilled into easy.
